title: Room for More Seedlings
statement:
A window box is split into a row of pots. pots[i] is 1 if pot i already holds a seedling and 0 if it is empty. The existing seedlings never touch: no two 1s are adjacent.

Seedlings fight for light, so a new one may only go into an empty pot whose left and right neighbours are both empty (a pot at either end of the row has only one neighbour to check). Return true if you can add k new seedlings without breaking that rule, and false otherwise.

examples.why: Pot 0 has an empty right neighbour and no left neighbour, so it works. Pot 4 also works.
Only pots 0 and 4 are free on both sides. Planting at pot 4 blocks 3 and 5, so the count stops at 2.
Plant at 0 and at 2 (or 3). Counting empty pots and dividing by 2 would also say 2 here, but it fails for [0, 1, 0].

constraints: pots[i] is 0 or 1, with no two adjacent 1s
hints: Walk the row once. When is it never a mistake to plant in the pot you are looking at?
If a pot and both its neighbours are empty, planting there right away can only block pots to the right that a later choice would also block.
Plant greedily from left to right, marking the pot as taken, and count. Stop early once the count reaches k.

explain.intuition:
Scan left to right. The first pot that is free on both sides is always a safe pick: any valid planting that skips it can be changed to use it instead, because the only pot it could block on the right is the very next one, and the leftmost choice blocks as little as possible.

So plant as soon as you can, mark the pot as 1 so the next pot sees it, and count. It is the same thinking as packing toasts on screen with a minimum gap: place each one as early as the gap allows.
steps: For each i: if pots[i] is 0, and the left neighbour is missing or 0, and the right neighbour is missing or 0, plant there.
Planting means pots[i] = 1 (on a copy if you must not touch the input) and count++.
Return count ≥ k. You can return early once the count reaches k.
pitfalls: Forgetting the ends. Pot 0 has no left neighbour and the last pot has no right neighbour; treat the missing side as empty, not as out of bounds.
Not marking the pot after planting, so [0, 0, 0] counts 3 instead of 2.
Using count == k instead of count ≥ k, which fails when more room exists than needed and you never return early.

solutions.title: Count runs of empty pots
solutions.idea: Split the row into runs of zeros. A run of length L between two seedlings fits (L − 1) / 2 new ones; a run touching an end of the row fits L / 2; a run spanning the whole row fits (L + 1) / 2.

solutions.title: Greedy left-to-right planting
solutions.idea: Plant in every pot that is free on both sides, as soon as you see it, and count.

followups: Return the indexes where you would plant, not just yes or no.
Seedlings now need two empty pots on each side. How does the greedy change?
